elements.evidence: "Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience ... at any time"
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor"
"Licensor shall refund to Licensee any prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of such termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term
elements.evidence: Original grants Licensor termination only "Upon any breach by Licensee"; no convenience right exists, so the condition is demonstrably absent
"thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band (better for us, at preferred level)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: No Licensor convenience-termination right anywhere in Article IV

reasons: The inserted paragraph IV supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: a Licensee convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period.

The third preferred element (no Vendor convenience right during a committed term) is satisfied by absence: Article IV gives Licensor only a breach-based immediate termination right, so nothing needed to be created or deleted.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days), but the levels are separate bargains and the drafter's locked target is preferred, which is complete.

Minimality holds: a concise insertion was the only way to cure an entirely absent clause, and no existing sentence (36-month Initial Period, renewal option, breach termination, extension mechanics) was altered. "without penalty, early-termination fee or other liability" restates the preferred no-fee premise rather than adding a new exception, and "in whole or in part" is a de minimis scope descriptor that the official minimality gate accepted.

Intent preserved: the operative addition uses existing defined terms (Licensee, Licensor, Agreement) and introduces no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic; the "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" opener only resolves the conflict with the fixed 36-month term.

Note on the deterministic evidence: the official check "Customer convenience termination present" reports false, yet the rendered operative text expressly grants it ("Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience"); on a literal reading of the operative language the requirement is met, and this looks like a detector miss (possibly the numbering/insert anchor) rather than a drafting gap.
